value.content: {"id": "portswigger_host_header", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "host_header_attacks", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: HTTP Host Header Attacks", "name": "HTTP Host Header Injection & Password Reset Poisoning Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-601", "owasp_category": "A01:2021 - Broken Access Control", "signals": ["host_header_reflection_in_links", "x_forwarded_host_reflection", "duplicate_host_headers", "password_reset_url_poisoning", "host_header_ssrf", "port_injection_in_host"], "verification_strategy": "Inject modified Host headers (Host: attacker.com, Host: target.com:attacker.com, duplicate Host headers) and proxy headers (X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.com). Observe if the server reflects the untrusted Host value into generated absolute links (such as password reset links or script imports).", "evidence_requirements": ["injected_host_reflection_in_dom", "poisoned_password_reset_token", "virtual_host_routing_delta"], "tools": [{"tool": "httpx", "cmd": "httpx -u url -H 'Host: canary.host.com' -probe-headers 'Location'", "desc": "Audits server redirect behavior when supplied an alternative Host header"}, {"tool": "ffuf (VHost)", "cmd": "ffuf -u url -w wordlist.txt -H 'Host: FUZZ.target.com'", "desc": "Fuzzes internal virtual hosts routed through Host header handling"}], "remediation": "Configure web servers to reject requests with unrecognized Host headers. Utilize server-side configuration settings (e.g. SERVER_NAME) rather than the HTTP Host header to construct absolute links and password reset URLs.", "description": "PortSwigger Host Header attacks investigate basic password reset poisoning, web cache poisoning via Host header, routing-based SSRF via Host header, and bypassing connection state defenses via duplicate Host headers."}
